text: Reviewer kills 'perturb raw EEG samples' as an L-inf gradient attack rebrand; invert: the LLM emits physiology-constrained edit programs (shift spindle density, inject arousal at t) on a symbolic event layer, and reward includes a plausibility term from a second frozen stager trained on a different cohort, so fooling is only paid when the edit is physiologically legal.
rationale: Novelty is in the token-level action space being clinical events, not sample-level noise; the cross-cohort plausibility judge is the piece pure-gradient work cannot do.

text: Reviewer says a 0.5B Qwen adds nothing over a random search over perturbations; invert: run the exact ablation as the headline, treat the GRPO'd LLM as a learned prior over which 30s epochs to touch, and report attack success vs edit budget against random and greedy baselines.
rationale: Turns the obvious weakness into the paper's main table; the LLM only survives if it beats search per unit of signal change, which is the honest claim.

text: Scoop risk: someone attacks a CNN stager with FGSM by next week; invert: attack the hypnogram, not the epoch, by asking the LLM to rewrite a tokenized night sequence (W N1 N2 N3 R plus SpO2 dip tokens) to flip a downstream clinical decision (AHI category, REM latency threshold) while staying within a per-night edit distance, making the target a clinical-outcome model rather than a stager.
rationale: Clinical-consequence targets are what a biosignal FM workshop cares about; epoch-level stager attacks are considered solved and boring.

text: Reviewer asks why a text model and not a small transformer trained from scratch; invert: reuse the tokenizer literally by learning a BPE vocabulary over discretized SHHS EEG band-power and SpO2 quantiles, show the merged tokens correspond to known sleep grammar (K-complex runs, desat-arousal couplets), and let the LLM's misdirection prompts operate on these named tokens.
rationale: An interpretable learned vocab is a contribution on its own and justifies the text-stack reuse rather than hiding it.

text: Reviewer says one target model is not a foundation-model result; invert: mine the adversarial edits found on SHHS against a target trained on MESA and vice versa, and publish the taxonomy of transferable blind spots (e.g. N1/REM confusion under EMG suppression) as the deliverable, with the GRPO loop as the discovery tool.
rationale: Transferability across two NSRR cohorts is the smallest thing that reads as a foundation-model claim rather than a single-model attack.

text: Reviewer says red-teaming without a defense is half a paper; invert: fold the LLM-generated edits back into the stager's training as an adversarial curriculum and report the stager's robustness gain plus honest accuracy cost, with the LLM policy and the stager alternating like a minimax loop, with the FEVER 'did it get fooled' reward unchanged.
rationale: Closes the loop the workshop wants and keeps the existing reward function untouched, which is the actual 30-hour constraint.
